description:
FILED s470bo (Opus, 2026-09-05) by the probe that widened #1178 (an inline
declarator inside a call argument).  PRE-EXISTING â it reproduces on da5c310,
BEFORE and AFTER the #1178 fix, so #1178 neither caused it nor cures it.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s470bo/m3.pl in the s470bo worktree):

    our $g = "outer";
    sub show { print "g=$g\n" }
    sub wrap { my ($v, $d) = @_; print "wrap[$d]=$v\n"; show(); }
    sub inner { wrap((local $g = "inner"), "local-arg"); }
    inner();
    show();

    perl 5.40.3   wrap[local-arg]=inner / g=inner / g=outer
    PCL           wrap[local-arg]=inner / g=inner / g=inner   <- the restore
                                                                 never happens

WHAT IS HAPPENING.  `local` is one of the four declarators
`Pl::PExpr::extract_declarations` strips (`my|our|state|local`), and stripping
it is right for `my` â the variable stays, the declaration is recorded, and
`Pl::Parser2` emits the binding from the recorded declaration.  For `local` the
recorded declaration is DROPPED on this route: the parenthesised argument is
lowered as an expression, nobody consults `declarations`, and what is left is
`$g = "inner"` â a plain global write with no dynamic binding and no restore.

So the value the CALL sees is right (that is why it looks harmless) and the
SCOPE is wrong.  The statement-level spellings (`local $g = "inner";`,
`local $g = 1 if â¦`) are handled by `Pl::Parser`'s own `local` path and are
correct; it is only `local` appearing INSIDE an expression that is lost.

RELATED: #1178 (same unwrap site) made the `my` half of this family work.  The
`local` half was already broken through the Statement::Variable arm, which
strips too â the s470bo change did not widen it, it only made the
Statement::Expression arm agree with an arm that is itself wrong for `local`.

FIX DIRECTION (not designed): the declarator that survives the strip must reach
a lowering that can emit the dynamic binding, which means the expression seam
has to be able to say "this sub-expression needs a `local` wrapper around the
REST OF THE ENCLOSING STATEMENT" â perl's own scope for it.  That is a
statement-level fact discovered in an expression, so the right shape is
probably a pre-pass in Parser2 that hoists an in-expression `local` to the
statement's own `local` machinery, not a new expression form.  Until then the
strip is SILENT: rule 12 would say announce it.

BAR when taken: the reproducer; `local` inside a call argument, inside a
ternary, and inside a list assignment; the statement-level spellings unchanged;
a guard row with the restore asserted after the call returns; corpus-diff; the
gate; the full sweep.

=== ADDENDUM (s470bo, same session) â the word does not merely lose its
restore, it is lowered to a CALL THAT DIES ===

Measured while making #1178 safe.  On the Statement::EXPRESSION route the
`local` word is NOT stripped (that is what #1178's asymmetry preserves), and
what it lowers to is:

    sub wrap { my ($v) = @_; return $v }
    my $r = wrap((1, local $g = 'inner'));
      ->  (pl-wrap (p-flatten-args (list 1 (p-list-ctx (pl-local (p-scalar-= $g "inner"))))))

`pl-local` is the ordinary "unknown bareword becomes a sub call" lowering, so
the program dies "Undefined subroutine &main::local called".  So the family has
TWO wrong answers, one per PPI class:

    (local $g = 1)          Statement::Variable    stripped -> no restore
    (1, local $g = 1)       Statement::Expression  (pl-local â¦) -> dies

and `perl-tests/multideref.t:220` is the second one: its `eval { @{1, local
$x[0][0]} = 1 }` dies with PCL's undefined-subroutine message instead of perl's
"Can't use an undefined value as an ARRAY reference", which is why s470
registered rows 47/49 as accidental passes.

So the fix owes BOTH classes one real lowering, and the acceptance bar gains
`multideref.t` rows 47/49 (they should stop being an accepted divergence when
this closes) and the `pl-local` call disappearing from every emission.


=== s473a MEASUREMENT + DESIGN (2026-09-07, Opus) â NOT ATTEMPTED, and the
=== next session starts from here, not from scratch ===

WHERE PERL PUTS THE RESTORE â probed, and it is NOT the statement
(scratch/s473a/probes/m2.pl, perl 5.40.3):

  sub inner { wrap((local $g = "inner"), "arg"); print "after-stmt: g=$g\n" }
    perl prints  after-stmt: g=inner        <- still localized
  sub blk { { my $x = (local $g = "B"); print "in-block: g=$g\n" }
            print "after-block: g=$g\n" }
    perl prints  in-block: g=B / after-block: g=outer

So the fix must open the localization so that it WRAPS THE REST OF THE
ENCLOSING BLOCK â which is exactly what the statement-level path already does
(Pl::Parser::_process_local_declaration emits the open and bumps
`_local_let_depth`, and the block's end closes it).  The machinery exists; the
missing piece is only the decision to use it from an expression.

THE SEVEN SHAPES, all measured on s473a's tip (perl vs PCL):

  wrap((local $g = "inner"), "arg")   restore LOST  (g stays "inner")
  { my $x = (local $g = "B"); }       restore LOST
  my $v = (local $g = "E") . "!"      restore LOST
  push @a, local $g = "P"             restore LOST
  my $v = 1 ? (local $g = "T") : 0    restore LOST
  my $r = w1((1, local $g = 'X'))     DIES: "Undefined subroutine &main::local"
  my $v = (local ${'main::g'} = 4)    restore LOST (the symbolic spelling, and
                                      s473a's #1260 fix does not reach it â
                                      this route never enters
                                      _process_local_declaration at all)
  local $g = "S" if 1                 CORRECT (statement level, unaffected)

TWO PPI SHAPES, which is why one fix is not enough (dumped s473a):

  wrap((local $g = 1), "a");   ->  PPI::Statement
                                     PPI::Statement (the parens)
                                       PPI::Statement::Variable  "local $g = 1"
  my $v = (local $g = 2) + 1;  ->  PPI::Statement::Variable
                                     ... PPI::Statement::Variable "local $g = 2"
  push @a, local $g = 3;       ->  PPI::Statement, with `local` a BARE WORD
                                     (no nested Statement::Variable at all)

The nested-Statement::Variable shape already has its `local` STRIPPED by
Pl::PExpr::extract_declarations, which is why it silently becomes a plain
global write; the bare-Word shape is NOT stripped (#1178's asymmetry) and
becomes `(pl-local â¦)`, a call to a sub that does not exist.  Both are the
same missing decision.

FIX SHAPE (a pre-pass, and it IS new mechanism â which is why s473a stopped):
 1. At statement lowering, find `local` declarators that are inside the
    statement's EXPRESSION rather than at its head.
 2. Extract their targets with the existing `_local_target_item` /
    `_local_list_items`, and emit the BARE localization opens for them (the
    `$init_idx < 0` branch of _process_local_declaration) â one open per
    target, bumping `_local_let_depth` so the block's end closes them.
 3. Remove the `local` word from the token stream, then lower the statement
    normally: the assignment then writes the freshly installed slot, which is
    what perl does.

THREE HAZARDS THE PRE-PASS MUST HANDLE, all of them reasons this is not a
ten-line change:
 * A `local` inside a NESTED BLOCK of the same statement belongs to THAT
   scope, not this one: `f(sub { local $g = 1 })`, `map { local $g = 1 } @x`,
   `do { local $g = 1 }`.  Hoisting those is a corpus-wide silent regression,
   so the scan must stop at any Structure::Block.
 * EVALUATION ORDER: perl saves at the point the `local` is evaluated, the
   pre-pass saves at the head of the statement.  They differ only when an
   EARLIER part of the same statement reads or writes the same variable
   (`f($g, (local $g = 1))`).  Probe it and either accept-and-document or
   place the open more precisely.
 * The symbolic spelling `(local ${'main::g'} = 4)` must reach the same
   pre-pass; s473a's #1260 fix lives in a branch this route never enters.

ACCEPTANCE when taken: the seven shapes above, the statement-level spellings
unchanged, the three hazard shapes (anon sub / map / do) unchanged,
ir-conform 136-local and 137-local leaving known-fail.tsv by edit,
corpus-diff explained file by file, the gate, the FULL sweep, and the
companion op/local.t + op/localref.t legs.  perl-tests/multideref.t rows 47/49
are named in the addendum above as part of the bar.


=== MORE SPELLINGS, s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20; found by the Deparse -p mutation run; probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/local-paren.pl, perl vs main 5316d666) ===
The family is `local` ANYWHERE BUT AS THE LEADING STATEMENT: every one of these is lowered as a plain assignment and NEVER RESTORED -- `(local $g = 2);` (a parenthesised statement, what Deparse -p writes for every local), `$cond and local $g = 4;` (an everyday idiom: `$verbose and local $| = 1;`), `my $v = (local $g = 5);`, `f(local $g = 6)`, `(local(@a) = (9)); (local $h{k} = 2);`, a paren local inside a for body / a do block, and **`(local $/ = undef);` LEAKS $/ for the rest of the program** (every later read slurps).  RIGHT today: `local $g = 3 if COND;`, `local $g = 10 unless COND;`, `local ($g, @a) = LIST;`.  One mechanism with #1243 item 2 and #1451.
subject: `f((local $g = "inner"))` â a `local` inside a parenthesised CALL ARGUMENT is lowered as a plain assignment, so the global is never restored
